evidence.text: Alex has an established diagnosis of epilepsy, currently of uncertain type.
We discussed three event types today: nocturnal convulsions, daytime staring spells and brief morning jerks. Alex and their partner report no other event types.
The last nocturnal convulsion was on 12 August 2024, with none since.
Daytime staring spells began in November 2024 and continue two to three times a week; I currently regard these as focal impaired-awareness seizures.

Brief jerks of both arms after waking began in December 2024 and have occurred roughly every two weeks, most recently on 10 January. I regard the morning jerks as epileptic, although their precise classification remains uncertain.
The staring spells and morning jerks have both been recurring during December and January.
We discussed adding lamotrigine, but agreed to defer starting it until the next review. This is a treatment proposal, not confirmation that Alex has taken it.
I requested a routine EEG today. It has not yet been performed and no result is available. This is the only EEG requested for Alex since 20 July 2024.
Their established epilepsy diagnosis remains, with the precise epilepsy type still uncertain.
The daytime staring spells are the events I called focal impaired-awareness seizures in January. They continued intermittently, most recently on 10 June.

After reviewing the home videos and the detailed history today, I now diagnose these as functional non-epileptic spells. This reinterpretation applies to the same staring spells from their onset in November, including those described in the January letter.
This is our first reclassification of any of Alex's events from epileptic to non-epileptic, and the decision was made today, 20 June 2025.
The morning jerks described in January remain epileptic in my assessment. They have continued roughly every two weeks, with the latest on 18 June.

There have been no nocturnal convulsions since 12 August 2024. Reviewing the history up to today, the morning jerks have been the only active epileptic pattern since December; the staring spells are a separate non-epileptic pattern.
Alex confirms that they have never taken lamotrigine. The addition discussed in January was not enacted.
The routine EEG requested on 15 January was performed on 10 February. Its report became available to our clinical team on 12 February and described no epileptiform abnormalities.
I requested a separate repeat EEG today to investigate the continuing morning jerks; it has not yet been performed.
This letter records the consultation on 14 July and does not update Alex's condition beyond that date.
Epilepsy remains the diagnosis, with its type uncertain.

The daytime staring spells remain classified as functional non-epileptic events, following the decision of 20 June. The earlier January assessment is retained in the record as the interpretation at that time.
Alex and their partner confirm that the morning jerks on 18 June were the last epileptic events before this consultation, with none between 19 June and 14 July inclusive.
The morning jerks were the only active epileptic pattern between 16 April and 14 July inclusive. No nocturnal convulsion or other epileptic event type occurred in that interval.
At the consultation Alex confirmed that they had never taken lamotrigine, including between 20 June and 14 July. The January proposal was never started.
The repeat EEG requested on 20 June was performed on 3 July. Its report became available to our clinical team on 11 July, before this consultation, and described no epileptiform abnormalities.
This is a different EEG from the study performed in February. There were no other EEG requests between 16 January and 14 July.
